summary: Media is broken down by the kind of content being made (still image, vector graphic, page, moving picture, 3D scene, sound, score, interactive work, web page, broadcast, language) and then by the transformation applied to it, following the ACM CCS 2012 split of Computer graphics (image manipulation, shape modeling, animation, rendering) and of Applied computing > Document preparation and Sound and music computing. Leaves were then checked against the media standards that define their inputs and outputs (ISO PDF/X and ICC for print, MPEG and SMPTE for video, EBU R 128 for loudness, W3C WCAG, EPUB, WebVTT and TTML for web and captions, MusicXML and MEI for notation, IPTC for photo and news metadata, XLIFF and TMX for translation). Seeds were kept except that 3D was split into modeling and animation versus rendering and effects, music notation was split from audio production, and social media was widened to public communication; all source codes are from memory.

open_questions: Speech recognition and OCR are modeled here as language conversions, but O*NET puts Voice recognition software in enterprise and health and OCR partly in enterprise. The editor should confirm that those domains model the dictation and capture workflows and point at media.language for the recognition function, or move these two tasks.

Grammar and style checking is handed to enterprise because it sits in Word processing and Spell checkers, but it is a well-benchmarked language task; it would fit naturally as media.language.grammar_checking if enterprise does not want it.

Real-time graphics interfaces (OpenGL, Vulkan, DirectX, HLSL) are placed under media.rendering_effects.real_time_rendering. Computing may claim them as programming libraries; the brief's rule that general tools live in their general home suggests computer graphics is that home.

Diagramming and mind mapping (Visio, OmniGraffle) are placed here as structured vector drawing. Enterprise's process-mapping capability will want Visio too; a product can be an example of both, but the node should live once.
Generative tasks (text to image, video, music) are added inside each media type rather than as a separate generative capability. The editor may prefer one cross-cutting node.
Media asset management could be enterprise document management; it is kept here because its metadata (EBUCore, IMF) and proxies are media-specific.
Several see_also ids point at guessed node names in other domains (for example operate.telecom_broadcast_plant, learn.immersive_training); they need reconciling once those files exist.
